selection_rationale: Highest novelty and strongest operational relevance: directly evaluates verifier-augmented agent vs LLM-only under fault-injection and adversarial intents, addressing core unresolved gap (G2/U1) with falsifiable outcomes and feasible compute budget; results yield actionable evidence about safety vs cost trade-offs for agentic NetOps.
unresolved_uncertainties: U1: Can composing LLM generation with deterministic network-verification (generate–validate–repair) produce end-to-end safety levels adequate for automated configuration deployment in operational networks?
U2: To what extent does human-in-the-loop oversight reliably prevent automation-induced incidents in NetOps, versus serving primarily as liability/approval ritual?
U3: Which evaluation metrics and protocols most validly capture operational correctness, safety, and trustworthiness for LLM-driven NetOps agents?
required_repairs_before_preregistration: Preregister the exact simulator and deterministic verifier implementations, versions, seeds, and provide validation tests comparing simulator/verifier outputs to known ground truth cases.
Formally define outage/impact metrics and decision thresholds (e.g., fraction of destination pairs losing connectivity, prefix reachability thresholds) used to label 'high-impact misconfiguration'.

Specify full agent/tool orchestration details: tool APIs, repair-prompt templates, deterministic model settings (e.g., temperature=0), retry policy, and prompt-preservation to permit causal attribution.
Add an ablation plan separating verifier-only, simulator-only, LLM-only, and full-agent pipelines to isolate sources of improvement.

Preregister latency budgets and operational-cost reporting; include rate-limit/error-logging and mitigation procedures (timestamps, provider error codes) to avoid biasing latency and model-call measurements.
